name: Tessera Corponation Distributed Triage Lattice
description:
The Distributed Triage Lattice is a deployable diagnostic and stabilization system consisting of twelve interconnected biosensor patches linked by a flexible conductive mesh to a central processing hub roughly the size of a deck of cards. When applied across a patient's body, the mesh network continuously samples blood oxygen, pressure at wound sites, core temperature, neural activity, and the bioelectric signatures of internal organ function, feeding all data to the hub which generates a real-time triage priority map displayed on an integrated micro-display or transmitted to a connected medic's HUD. The system diagnoses what the naked eye cannot see — internal hemorrhage, organ perfusion failure, shock onset, and spinal instability — and flags each condition with a color-coded severity rating and suggested intervention.

Tessera Corponation's background in ambient inference systems is evident in the Lattice's design philosophy: it is built not to replace medical expertise but to extend it across distance and sensory limitation. A single medic can deploy multiple Lattice kits on separate patients and monitor all of them simultaneously through a networked display, triaging mass casualty situations with a clarity that would otherwise require a full medical team. The mesh patches communicate through the patient's own bioelectric field, eliminating the need for wired connections and allowing the system to function through clothing, body armor, and even some cyberware casings.

The Distributed Triage Lattice is primarily issued to corporate mass-casualty response units, military medical contractors, and Tessera Corponation's own security medical staff, but has found significant uptake among organized criminal operations that run enough personnel to justify its cost. It is not a treatment device — it diagnoses and monitors, but the actual intervention must come from a human medic or supplementary equipment. Street-level operators often find its cost prohibitive, but those who do acquire one tend to build small informal triage networks around it, becoming indispensable to their crews.

cultural_context: Ownership of a Distributed Triage Lattice in the Underbelly is a significant status marker — it signals that an operator or crew is organized enough, and well-funded enough, to invest in systematic casualty care rather than reactive patch-and-pray. Tessera Corponation maintains restrictive licensing requirements that officially limit the device to registered medical contractors, but enforcement is spotty. The device has become associated with a class of professional street medics who have essentially become small-business operators, selling triage services to gangs and runner crews on retainer.

story_hooks: A Distributed Triage Lattice recovered from a crime scene is still transmitting patient data — someone with a gunshot wound is alive somewhere in the city, being monitored by whoever holds the linked hub. The data trail could lead to a survivor, a captor, or both.

Tessera Corponation's latest firmware update added a hidden logging function that transmits anonymized patient biometrics back to a Tessera server — a street medic collective has discovered this and is threatening to go public unless Tessera buys their silence or kills the feature.

A player character's crew is offered a Distributed Triage Lattice as payment for a job, but the device's previous owner is still listed in the system's user registry — and that person has been officially declared dead by a corporation that would very much like to keep it that way.
